newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Manuel sees 5.1 pct 1996/97 deficit, maybe less.
newsitem.headline: Manuel sees 5.1 pct 1996/97 deficit, maybe less.

text.p: South Africa expects a budget deficit of 5.1 percent of GDP in 1996/97 (April-March), and possibly less when final figures come out, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.
Asked if the government would better its 5.1 percent target in the current year, Manuel told reporters:

"We are still talking estimates. The harder figures come from different processes. It still is possible but at this stage we are saying that achieving that 5.1 percent has been remarkable...it does provide us with a basis for taking a big step forward to a four percent deficit."

The government's Growth, Employment and Redistribution (GEAR) strategy, published last June, set a target of a 5.1 percent budget deficit in 1996/97, falling to four percent in 1997/98, 3.5 percent in 1998/99 and 3.0 percent in 1999/2000.
Manuel is to present his Adjustments Appropriation Bill to parliament at 1230 GMT. The budget for 1997/98 will be presented on March 12.
